Subject: Acme on-prem pilot — initial architecture & exception asks

Team,

Acme has asked us to scope a limited on-prem pilot (single DC) to validate our Private stack integration with their SOC & networking controls. Before we commit a headcount or SOW, I need a quick cross-functional read on two things:

1) Architecture gating risks — what pieces of the runtime or orchestration require nonstandard network access, KMS/HSM integration, or special kernel/driver installs that we can't safely ship into a customer's DC?
2) Exception/contract asks — redlines they will almost certainly request around data residency, audit logs retention, and SLAs (they're asking for a 99.9% window in the pilot).

Specific asks: please reply with the following by EOD today if possible:
- short list of blockers (arch-level) that would prevent a pilot in a standard Acme rack (network egress locked down except a few whitelisted endpoints)
- a minimal staffing profile (roles + FTEs) required to onboard and support the pilot for the first 3 months
- any compliance docs we need to proactively surface (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, SAML config guide)

I attached the Acme questionnaire they sent and a blank network whitelist csv they asked us to fill.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Thanks Evelyn — high level responses inline below and a proposed approach.

Blockers (short):
- HSM/KMS: if Acme requires HSM-backed key ops that we cannot proxy, that will require us to ship a KMS connector and ~2 days of infra engineering + ops hardening.
- Kernel/drivers: our runtime currently expects CUDA 12.x drivers and a specific NCCL build; if Acme runs older drivers we either need to provide a containerized driver/install path (complex/legal) or ask them to stand up a compatibility host.
- Network: our auto-update/check-in beacon needs to reach our control endpoints for telemetry. We can whitelist endpoints but need explicit approval for telemetry metadata (we can obfuscate sensitive bits).

Minimal staffing profile (first 12 weeks):
- 0.4 FTE product/PM (owner, part-time)
- 1.0 FTE infra eng (initial integration lead, full-time for first 6 weeks)
- 0.5 FTE reliability/ops (on-call overlap, ongoing)
- 0.3 FTE security/compliance (evidence & SAML/KMS coordination)

Immediate deliverables I recommend:
- Fill the network_whitelist_template.csv and return to Acme (attached).
- Draft SOW v0 with clear exception language for driver installs and telemetry opt-in. I started a SOW draft (SOW-draft-Acme-v1.docx).

I'll loop in Acme security on the questionnaire — they should return the filled copy before we go deeper.

Kimberly

Quick technical read from runtime/infra:

- Driver compatibility: we can ship a containerized compatibility shim that includes the CUDA runtime and minimal driver helpers, but it requires host-level kernel module loads for nvidia-uvm; Acme will have to approve kernel module insertion or provide a host with nvidia drivers preinstalled. If kernel module load is prohibited, we fallback to CPU-only inference for the pilot (significant perf loss).
- KMS/HSM: two options: (1) proxy with TLS to our hosted KMS (needs explicit whitelist + inbound rules), or (2) implement a PKCS#11 connector to their HSM (3–4 weeks dev + 1–2 weeks of ops testing). Recommendation: start with proxy approach for pilot and revisit connector for production.
- Telemetry: we can provide a restricted telemetry bundle (tokenized request IDs + aggregated metrics) that omits request bodies. Ops will need a signed data processing addendum for that.

Resourcing note: to meet the 3-month pilot timeline with on-call coverage I estimate we need an incremental 0.6 FTE infra/ops for the pilot period (to cover integration work, vulnerability scans, and runbook creation). If legal/procurement review takes longer than 2 weeks, we should expect a slip in start date.

Rishi
